newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Corimon sees trade in its ADRs resuming by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Corimon sees trade in its ADRs resuming by yr-end.

text.p: Venezuelan paints and packaging company Corimon hopes that trade on the New York Stock Exchange of its American Depository Receipts (ADRs) will begin again by year-end, Corimon said.
"There isn't a definite date, but we're trying to get it by the end of the year," said head of investor relations Maria Gabriela Planchart.
The company was barred from trading on the NYSE in February after Venezuela's National Securities Commission (CNV) suspended trade on the Caracas bolsa.
The CNV recently lifted the trading ban after Corimon corralled creditors into a complicated restructuring plan that saw most of its $100 million in debt converted into preferred Class B shares.
Planchart added the company was studying the possibility of registering the Class B shares with the NYSE, but "it's still only a possibility."
